Man Buys New 2025 Rolls-Royce Spectre for $468,375, Drives 1,800 Miles, Sells for $360,000
22 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
The only thing worse than offering up your services and your wallet as an early adopter for EV tech is doing it when it comes to a very expensive luxury product. Since new, this 2025 Rolls-Royce Spectre has probably lost nearly $100,000 per year in depreciation, which means that in another couple of years, it's going to be a $200,000 car at best, depending on mileage.
Then you need to figure out the long term prospects when it comes to Spectre ownership. How much will this be worth 10 years from now? Less than a new i7 or Taycan? Conceivably. Although, for somebody looking for that Rolls-Royce experience, a used Spectre could make a great deal of sense. Yet, talking about such a car from the buyer's perspective seems a little too "on the nose". You've got to be hurting if you're the seller.
Again, with this Spectre in particular (a 2025MY car), the original MSRP stood at $468,375. The car was delivered new to the seller via Rolls-Royce Rancho Mirage in California, and driven only 1,800 miles before getting sold at auction for $360,000. Five years from now, this thing is going to be worth less than a Patek. Heck, it's already there, depending on which wristwatch model we're talking about.
So yeah, who could have known that in terms of depreciation, the Spectre would suffer the same fate as the Lucid Air ? This guy right here (I'm raising my hand), that's who. The range is borderline acceptable and so are the charge times (if you have access to DC fast charging), but those numbers are only getting worse with time. Its battery tech is already inferior to that of the Bentley Torcal, which is cheaper, faster and obviously more powerful.
But enough of that. I feel like I'm being a little mean so let's focus on some of the positives - like the spec of this car. Aside from the Black Diamond colorway, other noteworthy features include the adaptive LED headlights, a surround camera system, power-assisted coach doors, 23" seven-spoke wheels with self-leveling RR center emblems, Pirelli P Zero rubber, adaptive air suspension, active rear-axle steering, and more.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Phoenix Red and black perforated leather upholstery, Piano Black veneers, ventilated and massaging front seats, a black Shooting Star leather headliner, red leather door panels with Starlight illumination, quad-zone climate control, lambswool floor mats, black and red umbrellas, a head-up display, leather-wrapped steering wheel, and a 415-watt, 16-speaker Premium Audio sound system.
As for performance, you get a dual-motor AWD setup putting down 577 horsepower and 660 lb-ft (900 Nm) of torque. It can get you from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in about 4.4 seconds, with an EPA range of 251-277 miles. Or up to 530 km if we're talking WLTP figures.
It goes without saying that all those numbers look better in the Spectre Series II , which was unveiled earlier this year. It's got 18% more range to go with a 14% reduction in charging times. But rest assured that it'll go down in value just as rapidly as the original.
